_nguon: Stage 4.3 English overlay — day check against the Xie Ji Bian Fang Shu (Chinese quotes verbatim from the source fixture; English is an editorial summary in modern terms).

khung.tieu_de: Day check by the Xie Ji Bian Fang Shu
khung.phu_de: Adds the view of the Qing-era date-selection classic next to the everyday almanac: how the day's stem and branch support or check each other (Precious, Righteous, Controlling, Focused, Adverse), the eves of season changes, the Three Sha direction for digging and renovation, and the places where the book itself rejects baseless taboos.
khung.ranh_gioi: This is a cultural reference from an old book. Careful preparation of people, tasks and paperwork is still what decides the outcome.

bao.y_nghia: The book quotes the Huainanzi: a Precious day suits nurturing and helping things grow — today, caring for customers and your team, building up step by step.

nghia.y_nghia: The book quotes the Huainanzi: a Righteous day suits acting on principle so your name stands firm — today, keeping your word, signing clear agreements, following the rules.

che.y_nghia: The book says a Controlling day favours marching out — today, taking the initiative: clearing backlogs, fixing processes, negotiating once well prepared.

chuyen.ten: Focused Day (stem and branch share a phase)
chuyen.y_nghia: The book says a Focused day brings results when you see one task through, but avoids marching out — today, good for putting effort into one thing, not for starting a confrontation or dispute.

phat.y_nghia: The book says an Adverse day avoids attacking, marching out and seizing land — today, better not to start disputes, lawsuits or aggressive grabs; ordinary daily tasks are not mentioned.

loi.tu_ly: Four Separations day: the book sees it as the day yin and yang, and the five phases, part ahead of an equinox or solstice. The almanac only allows worship, bathing, haircuts, cleaning and small repairs; for other matters the book suggests another day.
loi.tu_tuyet: Four Extinctions day (the day before the start of spring, summer, autumn or winter): the book sees it as a season change. The almanac only allows worship, bathing, haircuts, cleaning and small repairs; for other matters the book suggests another day.
loi.thap_ac_dien_thuc: Folk almanacs list this as a Ten Great Defeat day (the day's Salary at {chi} falls into the void). By the book's own note, {dien} also sits at {chi}, so the Salary is filled — not a day to avoid.
loi.thap_ac_khong: The day's Salary at {chi} falls into the void, and neither the year, the month nor the Sun's position sits at {chi} — by the book's note, this is a true No-Salary day (Ten Great Defeat) that old almanacs avoid.
loi.duong_cong: Folk almanacs list this as a Yang Gong taboo day. Scroll 36 of the book explains these are just days of the Room mansion counted from New Year and rejects the taboo; whether to keep it is up to your family custom.
loi.tam_sat: The {huong} direction lies in this year's Three Sha zone (the {phuong} side). The old books advise against digging, demolition or major renovation on that side; the Xie Ji says a house may face that side but should not have its back there.

ngu_loai.sach: Xie Ji Bian Fang Shu · Scroll 5 (quoting the Dun Jia classic)
ngu_loai.y_nghia: A Precious day is the stem feeding the branch, a Righteous day the branch feeding the stem, a Controlling day the stem checking the branch.

phat_nhat.sach: Xie Ji Bian Fang Shu · Scroll 5 (quoting the Dun Jia classic)
phat_nhat.y_nghia: An Adverse day is the branch checking the stem; it avoids attacking, marching out and seizing land — today read as avoiding disputes and confrontation.

tu_ly_tu_tuyet.sach: Xie Ji Bian Fang Shu · Scroll 9
tu_ly_tu_tuyet.y_nghia: Four Separations fall one day before the winter solstice, summer solstice, spring equinox and autumn equinox; Four Extinctions fall one day before the start of spring, summer, autumn and winter.

tu_ly_viec.sach: Xie Ji Bian Fang Shu · Scroll 10
tu_ly_viec.y_nghia: On Four Separations and Four Extinctions days only worship, purification, bathing, grooming, haircuts, nail trimming, patching walls, sweeping, repairing walls and roads, pulling down ruined buildings and felling trees are allowed; all other matters are avoided.

thap_ac_bien_ngoa.sach: Xie Ji Bian Fang Shu · Scroll 5 (editorial note)
thap_ac_bien_ngoa.y_nghia: A No-Salary (Ten Great Defeat) day is avoided only because the Salary falls into the void; by the Liu Ren and Huo Zhu Lin methods a filled void is no longer void — so the ten days cannot all be called empty without looking at the year and month.

thap_ac_dien_thuc.sach: Xie Ji Bian Fang Shu · Scroll 5 (editorial note)
thap_ac_dien_thuc.y_nghia: Example: on a Jia Chen day the Salary at Yin is void; if the Tai Sui (year branch), the Month Builder (month branch) or the Tai Yang (Sun's position) is at Yin, it is not void.

tam_sat.sach: Xie Ji Bian Fang Shu · Scroll 3
tam_sat.y_nghia: The Xie Ji agrees with the Kao Yuan that one may face the Three Sha direction but should not sit in it, because that direction is disliked by the Tai Sui and not a place to dwell.

tam_sat_thong_thu.sach: Xie Ji Bian Fang Shu · Scroll 8 (the Xie Ji quoting the Tong Shu almanac)
tam_sat_thong_thu.y_nghia: The Xie Ji quotes the Tong Shu: when repairing a direction that a good star falls on, there is no need to check the Tai Sui, Three Sha, Guan Fu, Da Jiang Jun or other harmful influences.

duong_cong.sach: Xie Ji Bian Fang Shu · Scroll 36 (Correcting Errors)
duong_cong.y_nghia: People fear Yang Gong taboo days and the almanacs often list them, saying one should not travel or start things; the book says this comes from not knowing their origin, and so people are misled.

bien_ngoa_chung.sach: Xie Ji Bian Fang Shu · Scroll 36 (Correcting Errors)
bien_ngoa_chung.y_nghia: The yin-yang schools are mostly rigid, and what diviners invented is even more absurd.
